findings.title: No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock, so concurrent cold-start callers each reload the manifest
findings.body: The cache is read under RLock, the lock is released, and the write lock is taken without re-checking `entryPointAssetsCache`. Several requests can arrive while the cache is still nil, for example right after startup. Each one sees nil, then queues on `Lock()`. Each then re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` serially, and overwrites the cache with an equivalent value. This is the standard double-checked-locking gap. After acquiring the lock, re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. That way only the first caller does the work.

findings.title: File and network I/O is done while holding the exclusive lock
findings.body: `defer Unlock()` keeps the write lock held for the whole function, including `os.Open` and JSON decoding, and the CDN HTTP fetch if that branch is enabled. In Dev mode the early return never fires, so every call takes the exclusive lock and does disk I/O, and all concurrent page renders are serialized behind it. Only the final assignment to the cache needs the lock. The manifest could be loaded without it, then the lock taken briefly to publish the result.

findings.title: No regression test for the data race
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test. A test that calls `GetWebAssets` from many goroutines, run under `go test -race`, would show the race is fixed and stop it coming back. It could also check that the cache is populated only once in non-dev mode.
